main_text.p: omnes cerebri sinus obstruuntur: Sed ta-men neutram praecedit epilepsia ,nec con-sequitur. At media obstructionis pars pri-us tollitur quàm tota,quoniam quilibet si-nus cerebri prius ad dimidium usq; imple-tur,quàm totus. Propterea nulla epilepsia est dimidiata uentriculorum cerebri ob-structio. Adde quòd debili apoplexiæ pa-ralysis,succedit,non autem epilepsia, quë-admodum omnes docet experientia,& te-statur Galenus libro de Locis affectis quarCap.2.to.Quinetiam paralysis nullâ finit soluitq; epilepsiam,ueluti apoplexiam. Demum decrepiti senes, quibus crassus humor in cerebro abundat,paralysi,& apoplexia sæ-penumero corripiuntur,epilepsia uero uel nunquam,uel rarissime. Idcirco nullus co-mitialis morbus uentriculorum cerebri ob-structio esse uidetur.
main_text.head: EXERC. XXXIII.
UTRUM AB ALIQUA INTEM-perie possit oriri epilepsia?
main_text.p: PRimariam epilepsiam ab aliqua intem-perie cerebri posse fieri plusquam pro-babile uidetur. Nullus enim humor in cerebro diu consistere nequit,siue illic acer L[illegible, ~2 letters]uatus

page.notes: The large initial P is joined to "Rimariam" as "PRimariam". The subtitle is italic from "perie" on; the hyphen at "INTEM-" is printed. The last line reads "L" followed by a gap and "uatus"; the missing letters could not be read. The line "siue illic acer" is cut off at the scan edge, so the paragraph's final words are uncertain. The page number is printed "161" at top right.
